provenance.note: The twenty label placements were extracted from the Series 1 sheet's explicit transformation matrices, not from a product datasheet. That sheet was physically printed on real Avery 94106 stock and confirmed clean by the operator on 2026-08-11, so this grid is known to register on the operator's printer rather than inferred from a specification.
provenance.drift_note: The extracted values carried at most 0.1 pt of rounding drift from Avery's exporter (0.0014 in, invisible). The values here are the normalized figures with that drift removed.
provenance.unresolved: The extraction cannot settle which part of the 117 pt cell is bleed and which is die-cut. All content is therefore confined to the conservative centred safe area below, and a physical overlay proof on plain paper is required before label stock is loaded (KDR-21).

grid.numbering: row-major from the top-left: cell 1 is the first column origin paired with the first row origin, cell 20 the last of each

safe_area.note: KDR-13: all content lives inside this centred 100 x 100 pt box within the 117 pt cell.

derived_margins_pt.note: Margins of the derived grid with a zero calibration offset, as stated in IB0193. The effective margins after the offset above are computed by the layout processor and reported by it.

calibration.why_mm: The derived grid above is points, because that is what was extracted from the PDF and it must not be touched. This block is millimetres because it records what the OPERATOR measured on a physical proof, and round-tripping their measurement through a hand-converted point value is where a transcription error would enter. The layout processor does the one conversion, at full double precision.
calibration.sign_convention: x positive moves the layout RIGHT on the page. y and every row offset positive move it UP the page. guide_inset_mm positive pulls the die-cut guide INWARD from the cell box on every side. row_offsets_mm is parallel to grid.row_origins_pt and is listed TOP ROW FIRST; column_offsets_mm is parallel to grid.column_origins_pt and is listed LEFT COLUMN FIRST.
calibration.guide_inset_note: How far inside the 117 pt cell box the physical die-cut sits, measured by the operator on a transillumination rig. IB0193 R3 records that the extraction could not settle which part of the cell is bleed and which is die-cut; this is the empirical answer for this stock.
calibration.note: PRINTER calibration, not a correction to the derived grid. The column and row origins remain exactly as extracted from the physically verified Series 1 sheet and must not be edited to absorb these offsets; keeping them separate is what lets a run on a different printer reset calibration to zero without losing the provenance of the grid. IB0193 WP07.T03 anticipates this: report the observed offset, adjust, reproof.

history.after: first plain-paper proof; registration was good on the first attempt and this was fine-tuning

history.change: global x +1.5 mm (net -1.675 mm); row 4 up 0.5 mm; row 5 (bottom) up 0.75 mm
history.after: second plain-paper proof, read on a transillumination rig against blank Avery 94106

history.change: row 1 +0.5 mm up; row 2 +0.5 mm up; row 3 +1 mm up; row 4 +0.5 mm up; row 5 +0.5 mm up
history.after: Third plain-paper proof, read on the transillumination rig against blank Avery 94106.

history.change: global x -0.5 mm; guides +1.7 mm inward
history.after: Fourth proof: grid 0.5 mm left; die-cut guides measured 1.7 mm outside the actual cut on every side.
Fifth proof: whole grid 0.4 mm right. Operator called registration good at this point.

measured_through.scaling: printed at 100% with fit-to-page disabled; every emitted PDF also pins /PrintScaling /None (KDR-14)
measured_through.note: These offsets are only valid for THIS path. The calibration has absorbed the whole chain - the viewer's rendering, its scale setting, the printer driver, the printer, and the paper's behaviour through the fuser. Printing the same PDFs from a different application, or on a different printer, invalidates them: reset with -Reset and reproof rather than assuming they carry over.
measured_through.residual_scale: The per-row corrections fit a straight line with slope 0.382% and residuals under 0.15 mm, meaning the printed image runs about 0.38% tall over the page height - roughly 3 pt end to end. That is consistent with ordinary laser feed and fuser stretch, not with viewer scaling: a fit-to-page would have produced several percent, which is 8 to 16 mm of drift at the bottom row and would have been obvious on the first proof.
